newly_reproduced_gap: Starlette StreamingResponse commits HTTP 200 before the durable task result is known
a late durable transaction failure would otherwise end the HTTP-200 SSE body without a protocol-visible terminal failure
the predecessor wait_for(shield(task)) path can surface the task exception directly before reaching task.result(), so the old comment about later propagation understates the gap

properties: neutral stageb-commit-pending SSE comments are the only bytes emitted while the durable transaction is pending
client cancellation does not cancel the server-owned transaction
transaction failure is converted to one sanitized response.failed event with no exception text, provider/tool/call id, or successful response payload
a cancelled server-owned task is also projected as response.failed when the client remains attached
the complete canonical success projection is buffered before the first protocol event, so a projector exception cannot leak a partial success stream

cases: slow success: neutral heartbeat then canonical response
late transaction failure: sanitized response.failed after heartbeat
immediate transaction failure: response.failed without abrupt stream
projection failure: no partial response.created leak
client waiter cancellation: server transaction survives
ASGI StreamingResponse: HTTP 200 body contains deterministic response.failed terminal event
failure event contains server_error but no response id
simulated Codex retry is blocked from a second provider call by unresolved durable intent
cancelled server task becomes terminal failure for an attached client

codex_protocol_evidence.finding: current Codex parses response.failed whenever response.error is present; generic server_error is classified retryable
codex_protocol_evidence.implication: the bridge must not rely on the client to suppress retries. Durable unresolved provider_intent remains the duplicate-provider guard; a real Codex retry/restart proof on the final same-byte candidate is still mandatory.
